evidence: pam-logins-through-winbind @ templates/openvpn/pam_winbind.conf.erb:30: require_membership_of = <%= @comma_separated_groups %> renders P8TEST+p8testgroup under the params fixture (manifest lines 14-15: netbios P8TEST, separator +, groups [p8testgroup]); the probe runs the login service's auth+account stacks with pamtester: the member with the right password is accepted (rc=0), the member with a wrong password and the outsider p8testvpnout are refused, while wbinfo -a shows the DC accepts the outsider's password, so the refusal is the membership rule the line declares; the effect is a file the action wrote, not the action's own output

kerberos-realms-against-the-dc @ manifests/openvpn_domain.pp:40-47: /etc/krb5.conf is written from krb5.conf.erb, whose line 6 renders default_realm = P8TEST.example with the fixture's lowercase tld and whose only [realms] stanza is the literal DOMAIN.LOCAL (lines 8-14), so no KDC is configured for P8TEST.EXAMPLE and the client finds the DC's KDC through DNS; the probe greps the rendered default_realm, gets a ticket for p8testvpnin@P8TEST.EXAMPLE (rc 0, principal shown) and shows kinit in the default realm P8TEST.example failing with 'KDC reply did not match expectations' (case-sensitive realm); the credential cache is destroyed, matching mutates; that is what the referenced lines produce
